messages:
leo: Quick heads-up — us-east-1 shared GPU pool is at ~95% for the last 20m. Queue length is climbing and 99th-token latency is spiking. Looks correlated with large embedding jobs.

anita: Any noisy tenants obvious? Can we apply a temporary throttle while we investigate?

jamie: Yep — vectra-search is 6x baseline, consuming ~40% of batch slots right now. Pulling allocation logs + recent job ids.

chris: We should avoid hard evictions unless absolutely necessary. Proposal: implement per-tenant leaky-bucket pacing + dynamic min-share adjustments. Ramp the spike clients down to preserve p95 for others.

maya: Agreed. Prefer a pacing approach that ties rate to instantaneous free capacity. Example: leak_rate = min(config.rate_limit, free_slots * tenant_weight).

jamie: Draft config I tested locally: 
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "vectra-search",
  "pacing": {
    "algorithm": "leaky-bucket",
    "rate_tokens_per_sec": 50,
    "burst": 200
  }
}
```

chris: Add a grace window so the pacing auto-lifts when queue drops below threshold for N minutes. Implementation note: use Redis for token buckets + a small Lua script for atomicity.

deploy-bot: Canary applied to us-east-1 shared pool: feature=pacing.v1, traffic=5%, expiry=15m.

leo: Ops checklist: set alert if avg_queue_ms > 200ms or blocked_requests > 50 in 5m, run canary for 15m, then 25% rollout if p95 latency improves. Action items: jamie roll canary + collect metrics, chris add the auto-lift metric and Lua script, anita draft comms for customers who might see degraded throughput. @sre-oncall FYI.

jamie: On it. Starting rollout now — will post metrics snapshot at +15m.

maya: :thumbsup:
